rows.title: CachingMiddleware: operations after close() still succeed in memory
rows.test_src:
import os
import tempfile
import pytest
from tinydb import TinyDB
from tinydb.storages import JSONStorage
from tinydb.middlewares import CachingMiddleware


def test_caching_middleware_operations_after_close_should_fail():
    """Test that operations after close() should either raise or not persist to disk."""
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.json')
    os.close(fd)

    try:
        # Insert before close and verify it's on disk
        db = TinyDB(path, storage=CachingMiddleware(JSONStorage))
        db.insert({'a': 1})
        db.close()

        # Read the file content after close
        with open(path, 'r') as f:
            content_after_close = f.read()

        # Try to insert after close
        # This should either raise an error (preferred) or silently fail
        result = db.insert({'b': 2})

        # If no error was raised, verify the insert didn't actually persist to disk
        with open(path, 'r') as f:
            content_after_insert = f.read()

        # The file content should be unchanged (no durability after close)
        assert content_after_close == content_after_insert, \
            "Post-close insert should not be durable to disk"

        # Verify that db.all() after close also doesn't show the inserted data
        # when we reopen the database
        db2 = TinyDB(path, storage=CachingMiddleware(JSONStorage))
        all_records = db2.all()
        db2.close()

        assert len(all_records) == 1, \
            "Reopened database should only have pre-close data"
        assert all_records[0] == {'a': 1}, \
            "Post-close insert should not be persisted"

    finally:
        if os.path.exists(path):
            os.unlink(path)
